scenario.title: Faraday Development Ltd v West Berkshire Council
scenario.description: West Berkshire Council entered into a development agreement with St Modwen Developments Ltd for approximately £125 million, structured as a conditional land agreement. Faraday Development Ltd challenged the arrangement, alleging that it was in substance a public works contract that should have been competitively procured under the Public Contracts Regulations. The High Court initially dismissed the claim, but the Court of Appeal reversed this decision, holding that the agreement was indeed a public works contract and declaring its ineffectiveness.

interests: Compliance & Legality: Ensure the procurement process adheres to Public Contracts Regulations and Procurement Act 2023
Protection of Public Funds: Avoid delays and costs associated with re-running a £125,000,000 contract
Continuity of Service / Delivery: Deliver critical development project for West Berkshire residents without disruption
goals: Defend the procurement decision in accordance with law and evidence
Minimise delay and cost to public funds
ca_pre_negotiation.batna: Defend the decision in the TCC — costly (£50k+) and slow (6-12 months), with a real risk of automatic suspension.
ca_pre_negotiation.opening_position: We stand by our initial evaluation, which was conducted fairly and transparently. We are willing to provide additional information and clarification to address Faraday Development Ltd's concerns.

interests: Commercial Loss & Recovery: £125 million contract value at risk due to declared ineffectiveness of agreement
Protection of Reputation: credibility and win-rate targets impacted by public challenge and Court of Appeal ruling
goals: Force a re-evaluation of submitted bids
bidder_pre_negotiation.batna: Pursue a damages claim in the TCC — costly (£50k-£100k in legal fees) for a business our size, slow, and the outcome is uncertain.
bidder_pre_negotiation.opening_position: Request West Berkshire Council to reconsider their evaluation process and provide detailed feedback on the scoring methodology
legal_basis: High Court and Court of Appeal rulings

messages.message: We appreciate Faraday Development Ltd's concerns regarding the development agreement with St Modwen Developments Ltd. However, we must clarify that our evaluation process was based on the correct application of the Public Contracts Regulations. Could you please specify which particular aspects of the agreement you believe were not in compliance with these regulations?

We appreciate your clarification on the evaluation process, but we would like to request more specific information about how you applied the Public Contracts Regulations in this case. Could you provide us with a detailed explanation of the scoring methodology used for each criterion and any relevant evaluator comments? We believe that a thorough review of these documents will help us understand why our bid was not successful.

We acknowledge Faraday Development Ltd's request for detailed information on our scoring methodology and evaluator comments. We can provide a redacted version of the evaluation report, excluding commercially sensitive information, to help clarify our decision-making process. This will include a breakdown of scores for each criterion, as well as any relevant evaluator comments. However, we must emphasize that this documentation is subject to the Public Contracts Regulations and cannot be disclosed in full due to confidentiality concerns.

We appreciate your offer to provide a redacted version of the evaluation report, but we would like to request that you also provide a detailed explanation of how you applied the scoring methodology for each criterion. Specifically, could you clarify why our bid scored lower in certain areas despite meeting all the requirements? We are concerned that there may have been an inconsistency in the application of the scoring criteria.

We understand your concerns regarding the scoring methodology and would like to clarify that our evaluation process was based on a thorough review of each bid against the published evaluation criteria. We can provide additional information on the specific scoring for each criterion, including any relevant evaluator comments. However, we must emphasize that our evaluation team's decisions were made in good faith and in accordance with the Public Contracts Regulations. To address your concerns, we are willing to provide a more detailed breakdown of the scores for each criterion, excluding commercially sensitive information.

We appreciate your willingness to provide additional information on the scoring methodology and evaluator comments. However, we are still concerned that there may have been an inconsistency in the application of the scoring criteria. To address this concern, we propose a joint review of the evaluation process with an independent third-party expert. This would help ensure that our bid was evaluated fairly and consistently against the published evaluation criteria.
messages.proposal: A joint review of the evaluation process with an independent third-party expert

messages.message: We understand your proposal for a joint review with an independent third-party expert to ensure consistency in the evaluation process. We are willing to consider this option, but we would like to propose an alternative solution that could provide similar assurance without the added cost and time required for an external review. Would you be open to having our internal evaluation team re-evaluate your bid against the published criteria, with a focus on ensuring consistency in scoring?
messages.proposal: Re-evaluation of Faraday Development Ltd's bid by our internal evaluation team

messages.message: We appreciate your willingness to consider our proposal for a joint review with an independent third-party expert. However, we are concerned that re-evaluation by your internal evaluation team may not provide sufficient assurance on the consistency of the scoring process. We would like to propose a compromise: if you agree to provide us with a detailed breakdown of the scores for each criterion, including any relevant evaluator comments, and an explanation of how you applied the scoring methodology, we will consider withdrawing our proposal for a joint review.

ca_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: The final outcome is more favorable than defending in TCC court, which would have cost £50k+ and taken 6-12 months. We were able to resolve the dispute through negotiation without incurring significant costs or time.
ca_win_statement.win_statement: We successfully negotiated a re-evaluation of the development agreement, which has provided assurance on the consistency of the evaluation process. This outcome is a win for us as it avoids the potential costs and risks associated with defending in TCC court.
what_was_achieved: Provided a detailed breakdown of scores for each criterion, including evaluator comments
Explained how we applied the scoring methodology
what_was_conceded: Agreed to provide additional information on the evaluation process
Considered the proposal for a joint review with an independent third-party expert

bidder_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: The final outcome is a re-evaluation, which is a compromise between pursuing damages or formal TCC proceedings and achieving our desired outcome. While we did not achieve the complete withdrawal of the decision to declare the agreement ineffective, we were able to secure a re-evaluation, which provides some assurance on the consistency of the scoring process.
bidder_win_statement.win_statement: We successfully negotiated a re-evaluation of the development agreement, ensuring that our bid is reassessed against the published evaluation criteria. This outcome acknowledges our concerns regarding the potential inconsistency in the application of the scoring methodology and provides a more transparent and fair evaluation process.
what_was_achieved: A detailed breakdown of the scores for each criterion, including any relevant evaluator comments
An explanation of how the scoring methodology was applied
what_was_conceded: The initial decision to declare the agreement ineffective remains in place
No formal apology or acknowledgement of wrongdoing by West Berkshire Council

key_sticking_points: Inconsistency in applying the scoring criteria
summary.concessions_summary: The Contracting Authority offered to provide a redacted version of the evaluation report, a breakdown of scores for each criterion, and an explanation of how they applied the scoring methodology. They also proposed re-evaluation by their internal team.
summary.court_reasoning_summary: The Court assessed compliance qualitatively throughout the negotiation. In Round 4, it concluded that the Contracting Authority's process followed was False due to a manifest error in addressing the underlying issue of consistency in scoring.
summary.likely_next_steps: Re-evaluation of the Aggrieved Bidder's bid against published criteria by an independent third-party expert or the Contracting Authority's internal team. Alternatively, settlement negotiations may continue.
summary.plain_english_summary: The negotiation centered around concerns about the evaluation process and consistency in scoring. The Contracting Authority made concessions to provide more information, but ultimately, the Court recommended re-evaluation due to a manifest error in addressing the underlying issue of consistency.
